issues.t: Turbocharger leaks oil and smokes
issues.sym: White or blue-gray smoke from the exhaust that doesn't clear once the engine is warm, a check engine light (often code P0106), oil use, and in bad cases a loss of power.
issues.why: The bearings inside one or both turbochargers wear early and let engine oil leak through into the exhaust. Infiniti extended the emissions warranty on the turbochargers of 2017-2018 Q60s to 10 years or 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Don't keep driving with heavy smoke, since a failing turbo can damage the engine. Take it to an Infiniti dealer and ask about warranty extension P4A05/P4A06; owners who already paid for a turbo may be able to get reimbursed.

issues.t: Engine failure from sludge or bearing damage
issues.sym: Knocking, white smoke, overheating or a sudden seized engine, sometimes with little warning. Owners report this between about 39,000 and 80,000 miles.
issues.why: Some 2017 Q60 engines have failed with oil sludge or a spun main bearing. Dealers have sometimes blamed maintenance and denied warranty, and engine replacement is one of the most expensive repairs on this car.
issues.next: Change the oil on time with the correct full-synthetic oil and keep every receipt. If you hear knocking or see the oil light, stop the engine and have it checked before driving further.

issues.t: Airbag light from passenger seat occupant sensor
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on or flashes, and the passenger airbag status light may show the airbag is off.
issues.why: The occupant sensor in the passenger seat, which tells the car if an adult is sitting there, fails. On newer Q60s the dealer may say the sensor comes only with a whole seat frame, and owners report very expensive quotes.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read. The passenger airbag may not deploy while the light is on. Ask for a second opinion or a used or rebuilt sensor before paying for a full seat frame.

issues.t: Rough running from carbon on the intake valves
issues.sym: Misfires, a rough idle, stumbling or hesitation when accelerating, and gradual power loss, usually showing up after 80,000 miles.
issues.why: This engine sprays fuel straight into the cylinders, so nothing washes oily vapor off the intake valves. Carbon slowly builds up and disturbs airflow.
issues.next: Have a shop confirm with a scope before paying for it. Walnut-blasting the valves is the usual fix.

issues.t: Misfire from a failing fuel injector
issues.sym: Check engine light with misfire codes P0301-P0306, a rough idle and poor performance.
issues.why: Debris from the factory fuel rail can damage the injectors. Infiniti issued a bulletin and an updated rail.
issues.next: Have the misfire traced to a cylinder. Ask the dealer about the bulletin, and replace the rail along with the injectors if debris is found.

issues.t: Drive belt slips off the pulley
issues.sym: A squeal, then several warning lights, no A/C, overheating or loss of power steering.
issues.why: On early 3.0L twin-turbo engines the accessory belt can walk off a pulley. Infiniti addressed it with a service bulletin.
issues.next: Pull over safely if the temperature gauge climbs. Ask a dealer about the bulletin repair.

issues.t: Run-flat tires go flat or fail early
issues.sym: Repeated flats and tire pressure warnings, with tires wearing out quickly.
issues.why: Q60s came with low-profile run-flat tires that owners say fail often. One owner replaced ten tires by 48,000 miles, and these tires are expensive to replace.
issues.next: Check pressures monthly. Many owners switch to regular tires and carry a plug kit or inflator.

issues.t: Engine may stall from fuel pump software (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can stall while driving even though the gauge shows fuel.
issues.why: Wrong software in the fuel pump control module could leave too little fuel in the main side of the tank.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 17V476. The dealer reprograms the module for free.

issues.t: Backup camera image can be switched off (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera image doesn't appear when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: The display settings let the camera view be turned off and kept off the next time the car went into reverse.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer updates the software for free.

issues.t: Rear seat belt may not lock (recall)
issues.sym: No sign in daily driving. A rear belt may not hold properly in a crash with more than one impact.
issues.why: Some rear seat belt assemblies had a locking mechanism that may not lock as intended.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer inspects and replaces the belts for free.

issues.t: Engine may cut power after hard acceleration (recall)
issues.sym: After a burst of hard acceleration the car can lose power or stall. Owners also report limp mode at low speed.
issues.why: Engine computer software could cut power and fuel after it sensed rapid acceleration.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V234. The dealer reprograms the engine computer for free.

issues.t: Center screen and backup camera go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The center screen turns off, so the backup camera image doesn't show.
issues.why: A software error in the audio-video control unit can shut the screen off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V599. The dealer updates the software for free.

issues.t: Check engine light from oil pressure control wiring (P06DA)
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P06DA, which points to the oil pump control circuit.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB24-017 tells dealers to replace the engine room sub-harness when this code is confirmed active.
issues.next: Have the code confirmed and ask the dealer about the bulletin and any coverage before paying.

issues.t: Coolant seeping at the water pump
issues.sym: Dried coolant crust around the water pump, a sweet smell, or a slowly dropping coolant level.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB20-016 covers coolant residue at the water pump on these cars.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. Ask a dealer to inspect the pump using the bulletin before it starts leaking more.

issues.t: Tire pressure sensor leaks air
issues.sym: One tire slowly loses air and the tire pressure light comes on, with no nail or puncture found.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB20-003 covers tire pressure sensors leaking air at the valve on 2017-2020 Q60s.
issues.next: Have the tire shop check the valve stem with soapy water. A new sensor seal or sensor fixes it.

issues.t: Key not detected and car won't start
issues.sym: A 'key not detected' message and the engine won't start, or a new key won't program.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletins ITB13-052 and ITB17-060 cover intelligent key detection and key programming problems.
issues.next: Try a new key fob battery and hold the fob against the start button. If it continues, ask the dealer about the bulletins.

issues.t: Infotainment screen freezes, reboots or goes black
issues.sym: The center screens freeze, restart on their own or go black, sometimes taking the backup camera with them.
issues.why: Infiniti has issued several software updates for infotainment problems and, on later cars, steps for replacing the control unit.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check for the latest infotainment software. If the camera goes blank, get it fixed promptly.

issues.t: Emergency call (SOS) system fault
issues.sym: A warning about the SOS or telematics system, or connected services that stop working.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletins cover fault codes in the telematics unit, including its internal backup battery, and resetting the unit after a crash notification.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check the telematics unit using the bulletins.

issues.t: Engine software emissions update (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you notice. You may get a letter about an emissions campaign.
issues.why: Infiniti ran a voluntary emissions recall to inspect and reprogram the engine computer on 2017-2019 Q60s.
issues.next: Check your VIN with an Infiniti dealer; the update is free.

issues.t: Emergency braking or cruise radar warning light
issues.sym: The forward emergency braking or adaptive cruise warning comes on or blinks, and those features stop working.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletins cover warning lights and fault codes for these driver-assist systems. On one 2021 car the dealer found a cracked bracket holding the front radar.
issues.next: Keep the front radar area clean. If the light stays on, have the sensor and its mount checked.

issues.t: Check engine light for airflow sensor codes (P0101/P010B)
issues.sym: Check engine light with mass airflow sensor codes, usually with no change in how it drives.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletins ITB13-054 and ITB23-001 cover these codes; the fix may be an engine computer update rather than a new sensor.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to check for the bulletin before replacing the sensor.

issues.t: Retractable hard top stops working
issues.sym: The convertible's hard top won't open or close, or stops halfway.
issues.why: After the battery is disconnected or runs down, the top's controller can lose its settings and store codes B1707 and B1708. Infiniti issued a bulletin with the fix.
issues.next: Don't force it. A dealer can reset the top following bulletin ITB14-030; RepairPal owners report closing it manually after a battery disconnect.

issues.t: Squeaks and rattles from the hard top or trunk
issues.sym: Squeaking, buzzing or rubbing noises from the roof or trunk area over bumps.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB13-058 covers noises from the retractable hard top and trunk.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to follow the bulletin; it usually involves adjusting and lubricating seals.

issues.t: Power windows stop working right after a power loss
issues.sym: Auto-up windows stop working or windows don't close fully after the battery is disconnected or dies.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB16-042 says the windows need to be re-initialized after a power interruption.
issues.next: Try the window reset: hold the switch up for a few seconds after the window closes. A dealer can also reset them.

issues.t: Check engine light for slow oxygen sensors
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes P0139 or P0159.
issues.why: Infiniti bulletin ITB13-056 covers slow-responding downstream oxygen sensors.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the bulletin; the fix may be a sensor or software.

issues.t: Shift problems from the transmission valve body
issues.sym: Harsh or erratic shifts, limp mode and codes such as P0720 (output speed sensor).
issues.why: Owners of 2014 and 2015 Q60s report transmission valve body and speed sensor faults around 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned and the fluid checked. A valve body or sensor repair is far cheaper than a new transmission.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads fuel when the tank is empty
issues.sym: The gauge shows about a third of a tank and the car runs out of fuel.
issues.why: One owner ran out of fuel twice, even after the fuel pump and sending unit were replaced. Earlier Nissan-family cars had a recall for the same symptom, but this car is not covered.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups and have the fuel level sensors and gauge checked.

issues.t: Weak airflow from the dash vents
issues.sym: Little air comes from the dash vents, especially in the dash-and-floor setting.
issues.why: RepairPal lists weak dash vent airflow as a reported Q60 problem, most noticeable when both dash and floor vents are selected.
issues.next: Check the cabin air filter first. If it persists, have the vent mode door and its actuator checked.
